name: The Dylan Amsterdam
positioning: Boutique hotel in connected historic buildings on the Keizersgracht canal, in Amsterdam's 9-streets area
best_for: Travelers who want a canal-side base for exploring Amsterdam on foot or by bike
Guests who like individually styled rooms in a historic building

facts.text: The hotel is in the 9-streets area on the Keizersgracht canal.
The Keizersgracht, where the hotel sits, is the widest canal in the city.
The hotel is in Amsterdam's historic heart, steps from the Nine Streets, the Jordaan, museums and independent boutiques.
The hotel once opened as Blakes Amsterdam and is now a Leading Hotel of the World.
Guests enter through a small courtyard and a residential-style door.
Several buildings are connected by stairs and pathways, with tiny gardens or patios, seating nooks and cozy spaces.
The hotel has four different room styles.
Rooms have a B&O sound system, an Illy espresso maker and Aesop bath amenities.
Double Rooms in the Original building look over the garden; those in the Serendipity building look over the atrium.
The concierge team curates itineraries, from museum reservations and private art guides to countryside excursions.
Restaurant Vinkeles is situated in an 18th-century bakery.
Bar Brasserie OCCO is known for its High Wine, a take on High Tea.

highlights.text: The address was once home to the first theater in Amsterdam, dating back to the 1600s, before becoming Hotel Blakes.
The Luxury Duplex Room, known as a staircase room, is arranged over two floors connected by a steep internal staircase.
Hand-crafted Roetz electric bikes are available for guests to borrow free of charge.
The Junior Suites Canal View are in the Serendipity building, in Serendipity style with natural warming shades of brown and grey.
Turndown service delivers Amsterdam stroopwafels made by the nearby Lanskroon bakery.

considerations.text: The hotel does not have a pool; it has a gym and offers in-room treatments.
The city and the hotel are not easy to maneuver around for those with mobility issues.
WhataHotel notes premium pricing reflecting the luxury positioning.
